variants.name: Inline footnotes
variants.description: The sources leave the answer and become numbered superscripts inside the prose, with the numbered list moved beneath on hairline rows.
variants.guidance: Use when the answer is a paragraph rather than a list of findings, and the reader needs to know which sentence rests on which source. Each superscript is a fragment link to the matching row, so the claim and the source stay connected without a hover card. The superscript carries text-sm rather than the browser default, which is a relative shrink that lands under the 12px floor inside 14px copy. Keep it to three or four marks in a paragraph: past that the copy is reading as a bibliography and the stacked source cards of the default are the better surface.
variants.html:
A streamed run holds one HTTP connection open and sends each token as a text/event-stream frame, which is why a dropped connection resumes from Last-Event-ID instead of replaying the whole answer.1 The media type, the retry field and the reconnection rules are defined in the HTML Standard, not in a vendor SDK.2 A failure leaves the stream and returns as application/problem+json, the shape RFC 9457 defines.3

  1. [1] Using server sent events, MDN Web Docs developer.mozilla.org
  2. [2] Server sent events, HTML Standard section 9.2 html.spec.whatwg.org
  3. [3] Problem Details for HTTP APIs, RFC 9457 datatracker.ietf.org

variants.name: Flush rows
variants.description: The source cards lose their borders and become flush hairline rows, so the list can sit inside a card that already has one.
variants.guidance: Use anywhere the citations are rendered inside an existing surface: a chat turn, a result panel, an answer card. Three bordered cards inside a bordered panel is the nested box law 1 exists to stop, and a hairline row carries the same grouping for nothing. The domain stays mono and muted on the first line with the open action beside it, so the row is scannable before the snippet is read, and the snippet keeps text-sm rather than shrinking below the floor.
